artiest/willem-mengelberg.text:
Willem Mengelberg was born in Utrecht in 1871, the fourth of fifteen children of a German-Dutch sculptor. He studied piano and composition in Cologne and in 1891, at the age of twenty, became music director of the city of Lucerne. In 1895 he became principal conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra in Amsterdam, a post he held until 1945. Richard Strauss dedicated his tone poem Ein Heldenleben to him and the orchestra in 1898. In 1939 he conducted the premiere of Béla Bartók's Second Violin Concerto.

Mengelberg built up the Mahler tradition of the Concertgebouw. In 1902 he became friends with Gustav Mahler, who came to Amsterdam to conduct his own work. In 1920 he organised a Mahler Festival with nine concerts. Since 1899 Bach's Matthäus-Passion (St Matthew Passion) has been performed in the Concertgebouw every year on Palm Sunday. From 1922 to 1928 he also led the New York Philharmonic. His recordings with the Concertgebouw Orchestra stand out for the heavy use of portamento in the strings and for large changes of tempo. Admirers praise this; others feel it obscures the overall line. He was also regarded as autocratic towards his musicians.

His conduct during the German occupation is controversial. He gave interviews to the Nazi press and continued to conduct in Germany, but he also wrote letters to save Jewish musicians from deportation. In 1945 the Honorary Council (Ereraad) banned him from conducting in the Netherlands, a ban later reduced to six years. He withdrew to Switzerland, where he died in 1951. Mengelberg is regarded as one of the great conductors of the first half of the twentieth century, and at the same time as one of the most controversial.
artiest/willem-mengelberg.listen: Listen to his recording of Mahler's Fourth Symphony and notice the changes of tempo and the way the strings slide from note to note. Can you hear how freely he treats the tempo?

artiest/willem-van-otterloo.text:
Willem van Otterloo was born in Winterswijk in 1907. He began studying medicine in Utrecht, but switched to cello and composition at the Amsterdam conservatory. After graduating in 1932 he became a cellist with the Utrecht Municipal Orchestra and won a composition prize from the Concertgebouw Orchestra with his Suite no. 3, which he performed that same year at his conducting debut. In 1937 he became principal conductor of the Utrecht Municipal Orchestra. During the occupation that orchestra was placed under a German propaganda broadcaster in order to shield its members from the Arbeitseinsatz. After the war the Honorary Council (Ereraad) banned him from conducting until 1 May 1946 for this.

From 1949 to 1973 he was principal conductor of the Residentie Orchestra in The Hague, which enjoyed great success especially in the 1950s, partly thanks to a recording contract with Philips. He recorded extensively, with the Residentie Orchestra but also with the Concertgebouw Orchestra, the Berlin Philharmonic, the Vienna Philharmonic and the Vienna Symphony. He was known for his performances of nineteenth- and twentieth-century music. He also wrote music himself, such as a Sinfonietta for sixteen wind instruments from 1943.

In 1967 he became principal conductor of the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra and in 1971 of the Sydney Symphony Orchestra, where he remained until his death. He died in Melbourne in 1978 as a result of a car accident. His son Rogier also became a conductor and composer. Van Otterloo was one of the most important Dutch conductors of the post-war years, and he raised the orchestra in The Hague to an international level.
artiest/willem-van-otterloo.listen: Listen to a recording of the Residentie Orchestra under Van Otterloo and notice the clear, transparent sound of the strings. Can you hear how each section of the orchestra remains distinct and easy to follow?

artiest/willi-boskovsky.text:
Willi Boskovsky was born in Vienna in 1909 and entered the Vienna Academy of Music at the age of nine. From 1939 to 1971 he was concertmaster of the Wiener Philharmoniker. From 1955 to 1979 he conducted the New Year's Concert in Vienna, which mainly presents music by Johann Strauss II and his contemporaries. He was also principal conductor of the Wiener Johann Strauss Orchester until his death. He died in 1991 in Visp, Switzerland.

Boskovsky conducted with the violin in his hand, as a Stehgeiger, as Johann Strauss I and later Johann Strauss II had done. As a result his style appealed to many lovers of Strauss. He recorded a large part of the music of the Strauss family, on albums such as Welcome the New Year from 1971 and Die Wiener Philharmoniker spielen Strauss from 1974. He also recorded a cycle of ten albums with all of Mozart's dances and marches. His New Year's Concert of 1979 was Decca's first commercial recording made using digital technology.

In chamber music he led the Boskovsky Quartet, which together with a double bass player, a clarinettist, a horn player and a bassoonist formed the Vienna Octet. With the pianist Lili Kraus he recorded all of Mozart's violin sonatas, and with Wilhelm Furtwängler he played Brahms's Double Concerto. In 1979 he suffered a stroke, after which he withdrew from public life. Boskovsky gave the Viennese waltz a natural, light lilt and turned the New Year's Concert into a worldwide television event.
artiest/willi-boskovsky.listen: Listen to a Strauss waltz under Boskovsky and notice the position of the first violin and the slight delay on the second beat of each bar. Can you hear how the strings steer the dance?

artiest/william-byrd.text:
William Byrd, born around 1540 in London and died in 1623, is counted among the greatest composers of the Renaissance and had great influence in England and beyond. He possibly studied with Thomas Tallis, became organist and master of the choristers at Lincoln Cathedral in 1563, and in 1572 obtained a place in the Chapel Royal, the largest choir in England. In 1575 Byrd and Tallis were jointly granted the monopoly on printing music by the Queen. That same year they published the Cantiones sacrae, with seventeen motets each, a financial failure.

Byrd wrote in virtually every form of his day: sacred and secular polyphonic music, music for keyboard from the so-called virginalist school, and music for ensembles of strings and recorders or lute. He wrote Anglican church music, but became a Roman Catholic in the 1570s and afterwards also composed Catholic music, including Masses for three, four and five voices. His Cantiones sacrae of 1589 and the Three Masses are among his best-known works. His pavans and galliards and his consort songs show a secular side.

Catholicism brought him into difficulties: he appeared on lists of recusants who refused to attend Anglican services, received heavy fines and was suspected of contacts with conspirators. Around 1594 he moved to Stondon Massey in Essex, near his patron Sir John Petre, at whose home Masses were held in secret. Byrd made music for that small, hidden form of worship, and in doing so left behind a story of faith, risk and craftsmanship.
artiest/william-byrd.listen: Listen to one of William Byrd's three Masses and notice the voices following one another in long lines. Can you hear how the music sounds both tight and intimate, as if it had been written for a small room?

artiest/william-christie.text:
William Christie was born in Buffalo, New York, in 1944 and is a French-American conductor and harpsichordist. He studied art history at Harvard and, from 1966, music at Yale, with the harpsichordist Ralph Kirkpatrick. As a conductor he is self-taught. He taught at Dartmouth College, moved to the United Kingdom in 1970 and to France in 1971, partly out of aversion to the Vietnam War. In 1995 he took French citizenship.

In France he became known for his performances of Baroque music, in particular French Baroque. In 1979 he founded the ensemble Les Arts Florissants, named after the work of the same name by Marc-Antoine Charpentier. The great breakthrough came in 1987 with Lully's Atys at the Opéra-Comique in Paris. With the ensemble he recorded many little-known works by Charpentier, often for the first time, and further works by Campra, Couperin, Monteverdi and Rameau. Purcell, Handel and Mozart are also on the programme, including on the 1986 album Purcell: Dido and Aeneas.

Christie was a professor at the Paris conservatoire from 1982 to 1995 and in 2002 founded Le Jardin des Voix in Caen, an academy for young singers. He also designed the gardens of his home in Thiré, which became a protected monument in 2006. In 2008 he became a member of the Académie des Beaux-Arts. Christie brought French Baroque back to a large audience in the late twentieth century, with historically informed instruments and theatrical stagings.
artiest/william-christie.listen: Listen to Purcell's Dido and Aeneas under Christie and notice the harpsichord and the low strings in the accompaniment. Can you hear how they follow the singers continually?

artiest/william-herbert-brewster.text:
William Herbert Brewster was born in Somerville, Tennessee, in 1897 and was a Baptist minister and an important composer of gospel music. He graduated from Roger Williams College in Nashville in 1922 and settled in Memphis in the 1920s. From 1930 until his death in 1987 he was pastor of the East Trigg Avenue Baptist Church in South Memphis. He was also a poet, playwright, orator and leader in the civil rights movement.

He owes his lasting fame to his music. He published more than two hundred songs. Move On Up a Little Higher became Mahalia Jackson's first hit in 1948, and Surely, God Is Able became a hit for The Ward Singers in 1950. Both records are regarded as the first Black gospel records to sell a million copies. Other songs include Lord I've Tried for The Soul Stirrers, I'm Climbing Higher and Higher for Marion Williams and Let Us Go Back to the Old Landmark, which is a favourite in Black gospel choirs. Brewster also wrote more than fifteen gospel music dramas, including From Auction Block to Glory from 1941, the first nationally staged African American religious play with gospel songs written especially for it.

The young Elvis Presley also sometimes went to his church and listened to his sermons, which were broadcast on Sunday evenings over Memphis radio under the name Camp Meeting of the Air. Brewster preached that a better day would come when all people would walk as brothers. In 1982 the Smithsonian Institution honoured him. He died in Memphis in 1987. Brewster brought the gospel song to a large audience and left his mark on the world of rock 'n' roll.
artiest/william-herbert-brewster.listen: Listen to Move On Up a Little Higher as performed by Mahalia Jackson and notice the singing growing higher and more powerful each time. Can you hear how the text about climbing is portrayed in the melody itself?

artiest/william-walton.text: William Walton, from Oldham, was one of the most important British concert composers. He also wrote for film, most often for Laurence Olivier. For Olivier's Shakespeare films Henry V (1944), Hamlet (1948) and Richard III (1955) he wrote music with solemn marches, old English dances and broad melodies. The charge at Agincourt in Henry V is built on a large crescendo in the orchestra. With Battle of Britain (1969) things went wrong. The studio replaced almost his entire score with music by Ron Goodwin. Only the piece Battle in the Air remained in the film.
artiest/william-walton.listen: Notice the brass fanfares and march rhythms set against soft, archaic string music that points to old English music.

artiest/willie-bobo.text:
Willie Bobo, whose real name was William Correa, was born in 1934 into a Puerto Rican family in Spanish Harlem, New York. His father played the cuatro. As a teenager he taught himself bongos, congas, timbales and drums. In 1947 he started as a band boy for Machito, so that he could attend the concerts for free, and sometimes stood in on percussion. He learned from Mongo Santamaría, for whom he interpreted, and recorded in the early 1950s with Mary Lou Williams, who gave him the nickname Bobo.

From 1954 to 1957 he played in Tito Puente's orchestra, then with George Shearing, on the album The Shearing Spell. Later he played with the vibraphonist Cal Tjader, in the Modern Mambo Quintet. In 1960 he made the album Sabroso! with Santamaría. He also recorded under his own name, with records such as Do That Thing/Guajira. His breakthrough came in 1965 with his contribution to Cal Tjader's Soul Sauce and then at Verve with Spanish Grease, whose title song became his best-known number.

Bobo rejected the stereotyped expectations of Latin music and moved smoothly between Latin, jazz and rhythm and blues, as an authentic percussionist and as a jazz drummer. In 1969 he moved to Los Angeles and became a studio musician, among other things for Carlos Santana, whose band covered Evil Ways in 1969, and played in Bill Cosby's band. He died of cancer in 1983, aged 49. His son Eric is a percussionist with Cypress Hill. Bobo linked the New York Latin scene with the jazz and soul of the 1960s.
artiest/willie-bobo.listen: Listen to Spanish Grease and notice the congas and timbales beneath the horns and guitar. Can you hear how the Latin rhythm and the rhythm-and-blues groove blend into one another?

artiest/willie-colon.text:
Willie Colón was born in the South Bronx in New York in 1950, the son of Puerto Rican parents. He began on trumpet and switched to trombone, inspired by the all-trombone sound of Mon Rivera and Barry Rogers. At fifteen he signed with Fania Records, and at seventeen he recorded his first album, which sold more than three hundred thousand copies. The producer Johnny Pacheco recommended the singer Héctor Lavoe to him. Colón died in 2026.

Colón was a pioneer of salsa and one of the key figures of the New York scene around Fania. He combined jazz, rock and salsa with rhythms from Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and Brazil. On records such as El malo, The Hustler and Cosa nuestra from 1968 and 1969 he deliberately adopted a gangster image, before that became common in the culture. With Lavoe he made, among other things, Aguanilé, and he also collaborated with Celia Cruz, Ismael Miranda and Rubén Blades. The album Siembra with Blades is regarded as the best-selling salsa album. His Christmas album Asalto navideño, from 1971 or 1972, lets the Puerto Rican diaspora in New York speak to the island, lovingly but also defiantly.

The relationship between Puerto Rico and the United States is a recurring theme in his lyrics. He was also active in New York politics, among other things as an aide to Mayor David Dinkins, and worked as an actor. In 2004 he received a Lifetime Achievement Award from the Latin Recording Academy. Colón brought the trombone to the fore in salsa, with a raw, sharp sound, and turned the Spanish-language street story into a sound recognised worldwide.
artiest/willie-colon.listen: Listen to Aguanilé with Héctor Lavoe and notice the raw trombones and the singing set against them. Can you hear how the brass and the voice answer each other?

artiest/willie-colon-en-ruben-blades.text:
Willie Colón was born in the South Bronx in New York in 1950, the son of Puerto Rican parents. He began on trumpet, switched to trombone and at fifteen signed with Fania Records. At seventeen he made his first album, which sold more than three hundred thousand copies. The Fania producer Johnny Pacheco recommended the singer Héctor Lavoe to him. Colón was a trombonist, but also a singer, composer, producer and actor, and he was regarded as a pioneer of New York salsa. He died in 2026.

Colón combined jazz, rock and salsa with rhythms from Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and Brazil. In his lyrics he described the lives of Puerto Ricans on the American mainland, and on his record sleeves he adopted the look of a gangster, even before that became usual. He collaborated with Ismael Miranda, Celia Cruz and the singer-songwriter Rubén Blades. Their album Siembra from 1978 contains Pedro Navaja, a song by Blades about a street criminal in the city.

Salsa from New York was urban music with strong brass, hard-hitting percussion and lyrics about everyday life in the barrio. Colón and Blades show that this music could be more than dance music: it also told stories about the street.
artiest/willie-colon-en-ruben-blades.listen: Listen to Pedro Navaja and notice how the song begins as a story while the rhythm section plays on unperturbed. What happens to the characters?

artiest/willie-nelson.text:
Willie Nelson was born in Abbott, Texas, in 1933 and grew up with his grandparents, who taught him music. At six he was given a guitar, and at seven he wrote his first song. As a teenager he sang in honky-tonks, worked as a disc jockey and in the 1950s wrote songs that became country standards: Funny How Time Slips Away, Hello Walls, Pretty Paper and Crazy, which became a big hit for Patsy Cline. In 1960 he moved to Nashville, played bass in Ray Price's band and in 1962 recorded his first album, ...And Then I Wrote.

Nashville proved too businesslike for him. In 1972 he settled in Austin, where the hippie scene gave him new life. With albums such as Shotgun Willie in 1973 and above all Red Headed Stranger in 1975 he became a leading figure of outlaw country, a reaction against the tight Nashville production style. In 1975 Wanted! The Outlaws was released, with Waylon Jennings, Jessi Colter and Tompall Glaser. Stardust from 1978 brought standards in his own loose style. Later he sang On the Road Again and Pancho and Lefty and, with Jennings, Johnny Cash and Kris Kristofferson, formed the supergroup The Highwaymen.

In 1985 he helped found Farm Aid, a concert for American farmers. In 1990 the tax authorities seized his possessions over a tax debt, which he paid off with the proceeds of the album The IRS Tapes. Nelson turned country into an open genre in which jazz, folk and pop fitted, with a drawling vocal style and a worn-out guitar as his trademarks.
artiest/willie-nelson.listen: Listen to Crazy in Willie Nelson's own version and notice how he lets the melody lag behind the beat. Can you hear how that free singing makes a familiar song sound new?

artiest/willie-the-lion-smith.text:
Willie Smith, nicknamed The Lion, was born in Goshen, New York, in 1893 and grew up in Newark. As a child his mother taught him songs on a broken organ, and with a prize won in a competition he got a piano of his own. From the early 1910s he played in clubs in New York and Atlantic City. In the First World War he served as an artilleryman in France, and his nickname is said to date from that time: his colonel called him a lion with his gun.

After the war he played in the clubs and at the rent parties of Harlem. Together with James P. Johnson and Fats Waller he developed stride piano, a style that grew out of ragtime, with a leaping left hand and fast, ornamented improvisations in the right. In the 1940s he found a wider audience and until 1971 he toured North America and Europe. In 1964 his memoirs Music on My Mind were published. Duke Ellington wrote Portrait of the Lion in 1939 as a tribute to him and called him a great influence.

For the history of pop, Smith is important as one of the voices of the Harlem piano school, from which swing and modern jazz later emerged. He died in 1973.
artiest/willie-the-lion-smith.listen: Listen to Echoes of Spring and notice the pianist's left hand, which keeps leaping back and forth between low bass notes and chords. Can you hear how light and elegant that sounds?

artiest/willy-william.text:
Willy William is a French DJ, producer and rapper, born in Fréjus in 1981. His father comes from Guadeloupe and his mother from Eritrea. He grew up in Champagné, in the Sarthe department. In 2003 he made his name with the club hit B Boyz Shake da Body, made with DJ Flex. In 2004 he produced Tragedie under the name Lord William. He then joined the French collective Collectif Métissé, which scored summer hits with cheerful, melodic songs, and made work of his own.

William collaborated with many artists, as a producer and as a guest vocalist. He made the charts with DJ Assad, Les Jumo, Keen'V and Ridsa. His big French hit came in 2015 or 2016 with Ego, produced and sung by himself, the main single from the album Une seule vie. Ego reached the charts of France, Italy, Germany, Belgium and Poland, among others, and in the Netherlands reached number four in the Top 40.

In 2017 he became internationally known with Mi Gente, a collaboration with the Colombian star J Balvin. A version with Beyoncé followed. The song won a Latin Billboard Music Award and in 2018 an MTV Video Music Award for best Latin video, and spent twelve weeks at number one on Spotify's global chart. In 2018 he also co-wrote and sang on Goodbye by David Guetta and Jason Derulo with Nicki Minaj. Willy William showed that a French club producer with a Latin American sound could reach the whole world.
artiest/willy-william.listen: Listen to Mi Gente and notice the rhythm that comes from reggaeton and the repeated, sing-song phrases that you can sing along to at once. What is left of the club when the vocals drop out?

artiest/wim-sonneveld.text:
Wim Sonneveld was born in Utrecht in 1917. His mother died when he was five. As a boy he already sang in an amateur choir, and in 1934 he formed a duo with Fons Goossens. Later he lived in Amsterdam, played small roles, sang chansons and in 1937 performed in cabarets in France. After the outbreak of the war he returned to the Netherlands. In 1943 he founded his own company, Rim Ram, with which he staged a large number of programmes until 1959. Cabaret Wim Sonneveld followed.

In 1960 he played the role of Professor Higgins in the Dutch version of the musical My Fair Lady. He brought the show to the Netherlands after a visit to America and played the part in 702 performances. After that he went solo, including with television shows and the full-length stage show Een avond met Wim Sonneveld in 1964. His songs include Het dorp, an adaptation of La montagne. He died in 1974 after two heart attacks.

Sonneveld is regarded, together with Toon Hermans and Wim Kan, as one of the three greats of Dutch cabaret. He was considered subtler and more complex than Hermans, and became a cultural icon of theatre, musical and song. In the story of Nederpop in School of Rock he stands at the origin, together with Hermans and Jules de Corte, as one of the great names from the time when the Dutch song still came out of the theatre.
artiest/wim-sonneveld.listen: Listen to Het dorp by Wim Sonneveld. Notice how the song's story is told with very little accompaniment and how the singing slowly grows more intense.

artiest/wimme-saari.text:
Wimme Saari was born in Kelottijärvi, in Finnish Lapland, in 1959, the son of a reindeer herder. He is a Sámi joiker, a singer of the joik, the ancient singing tradition of the Sámi. He became familiar with the joik at an early age and wrote his first joik of his own at fifteen. When in 1986 he began working for a Finnish broadcaster, looking after the record archives, he found a recording from 1963 of his uncle singing a joik. That led him to study the vocal art more seriously.

His breakthrough came when he began working with RinneRadio, a Finnish electronic group. He combines the traditional joik with his own improvisations, usually over techno and ambient accompaniment. His first album Wimme was released in 1995 and was voted Finnish folk album of the year. Gierran followed in 1997, Cugu in 2000 and Bárru in 2003, which includes Rievssat, and Gapmu, which is entirely a cappella. In 1996 he received the Áillohaš Music Prize, a Sámi music prize. He also sang on records by Hedningarna, Nits and Hector Zazou and appeared in films.

Wimme shows that a centuries-old, almost spoken-sung vocal tradition can go well with modern electronics. For many listeners outside Scandinavia he was the first introduction to the joik.
artiest/wimme-saari.listen: Listen to Rievssat and notice how the voice, without words that carry meaning in the usual sense, sounds almost like an instrument. Can you hear which electronic sounds lie beneath it and which do not?

artiest/wings.text:
Wings was a British rock band that existed from 1971 to 1981, formed in London by Paul McCartney after the break-up of The Beatles. The core consisted of McCartney on vocals and bass, his wife Linda on keyboards and Denny Laine, formerly of The Moody Blues, on guitar and vocals. Three lead guitarists and four drummers came and went, but the trio stayed together. The first album, Wild Life from 1971, was received moderately, as was Red Rose Speedway from 1973.

The breakthrough came with Band on the Run from 1973, recorded in Lagos, Nigeria, after two band members had left. The album reached number one in the United States and Britain and produced Jet and the title song. Live and Let Die, the title song of a Bond film, had already been a worldwide hit. Venus and Mars from 1975 contained Listen to What the Man Said, and Wings at the Speed of Sound from 1976 Silly Love Songs and Let 'Em In. In 1977 came Mull of Kintyre, the only British number one and one of the best-selling singles in Britain.

Back to the Egg from 1979 did less well. After McCartney's arrest in Japan the band lay dormant, and in 1981 Wings came to an end. In total the group had six number one singles on the Billboard Hot 100. Wings showed that, after The Beatles, McCartney could reach an audience of his own with an ordinary band and a rich, melodic repertoire.
artiest/wings.listen: Listen to Band on the Run and notice the three parts of the song, which differ from one another in tempo and mood. Can you hear how the song suddenly goes in another direction halfway through?

artiest/within-temptation.text:
Within Temptation is a Dutch symphonic metal band, formed in April 1996 by the singer Sharon den Adel and the guitarist Robert Westerholt, who are also a couple. Westerholt came from the band The Circle. Together with a few former bandmates they first started the doom metal group The Portal, but even before the first recordings they changed the name to Within Temptation. The debut album Enter (1997) was slow and gloomy, with gothic metal, slow keyboard parts and growls alongside Den Adel's clear voice. With it the band became known in the Dutch underground scene and played at Dynamo Open Air.

With Mother Earth (2000) the band chose a different direction: the growls disappeared and the music became more bombastic, with Celtic influences. After an appeal to fans, the video for Ice Queen was heavily requested on the music channel The Box, and in 2002 the song became a hit. The Silent Force (2004) and The Heart of Everything (2007) reached number 1 in the Netherlands and also broke through abroad, especially in Germany. In 2008 the band played in Ahoy with the Metropole Orkest. Later albums such as The Unforgiving (2011), Hydra (2014), Resist (2019) and Bleed Out (2023) added industrial and electronic influences, among other things.

Within Temptation combines heavy metal guitars with orchestral arrangements, choirs and Den Adel's classical-sounding voice. The band often won the Conamus Export Prize for the best-selling Dutch artist abroad, and is thereby one of the most successful Dutch bands outside its own borders.
artiest/within-temptation.listen: Listen to Mother Earth and notice how Sharon den Adel's clear, high voice rises above the heavy guitars. Hear how keyboards and orchestral sounds give the song a grand, almost cinematic character.

artiest/wizkid.text:
Wizkid, who was born Ayodeji Balogun in 1990 in Ojuelegba, a district of Lagos, is a Nigerian singer and songwriter. He began recording at eleven, in a group with friends from his church, and grew up on the music of King Sunny Adé, Fela Kuti and Bob Marley. In 2009 he signed with Empire Mates Entertainment. His debut album Superstar came out in 2011, with the single Holla at Your Boy, and in 2014 Ayo followed.

His international breakthrough came in 2016 with One Dance, a collaboration with Drake that reached number one on the American Billboard Hot 100. In 2017 he signed with RCA Records and Sounds from the Other Side was released. In 2019 he contributed to Brown Skin Girl on Beyoncé's The Lion King: The Gift. Made in Lagos from 2020 contains Essence with Tems, the first Nigerian song on the Billboard Hot 100. A remix with Justin Bieber took it into the top ten. More Love, Less Ego followed in 2022 and Morayo in 2024.

His music mixes Afrobeats, Afropop, R&B, reggae and dancehall. Wizkid is one of the faces of the Afrobeats movement that broke through worldwide in the 2010s, and shows that pop music from Lagos can compete in the Western charts too.
artiest/wizkid.listen: Listen to Essence and notice the calm, swaying groove and the soft voices of Wizkid and Tems. Can you hear how the rhythm slowly gets you moving, without anything coming at you?

artiest/wolf-biermann.text:
Wolf Biermann was born in Hamburg in 1936. His father, a Jewish resistance fighter, was murdered in Auschwitz in 1943. At seventeen Wolf moved to East Germany, because he wanted to put his communist ideals into practice there. In Berlin he studied political economy, philosophy and mathematics and from 1957 to 1959 worked at the Berliner Ensemble. In 1960 he met the composer Hanns Eisler, who took him on as a protégé. Biermann wrote poems and songs and sang them with his guitar.

Although he was a convinced communist, the regime was alarmed by his independent views. In 1963 he was refused membership of the ruling party. His programme about the building of the Berlin Wall was banned. His records appeared in the West, such as Chausseestraße 131 from 1969, recorded in his own flat in East Berlin, with street noise in the background and sarcastic, pointed German lyrics. They found their way back to East Germany clandestinely. In 1976 he was allowed to go on tour in West Germany, after which the government stripped him of his citizenship. Famous East German intellectuals protested, among them Christa Wolf.

Biermann is best known for the song Ermutigung from 1968. His music is that of a songwriter with a guitar, close to poetry and to political criticism. In this way he became a symbol of the dissident who was no longer allowed to perform in the Eastern Bloc. In the story of rock behind the Iron Curtain he appears as the singer who had not been allowed to play in his own country for years.
artiest/wolf-biermann.listen: Listen to Chausseestraße 131, the record Biermann made at home. Notice the bare guitar sound, the street noises in the background and how sharply the singing delivers the words.

artiest/wolfgang-amadeus-mozart.text: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart travelled across Europe as a child prodigy and in 1781 settled in Vienna as a freelance musician. He mastered every genre of his time, but it was above all in opera that he brought characters to life musically. In Don Giovanni from 1787, at the end the statue of the murdered Commendatore comes to fetch the seducer, with the menacing chords from the overture. He died in 1791 at the age of thirty-five and left his Requiem unfinished.
artiest/wolfgang-amadeus-mozart.listen: Listen to the scene with the Commendatore and hear how heavy chords and trombones announce the voice of a dead man.

artiest/wolfman-jack.text:
Wolfman Jack was the stage name of Robert Weston Smith, an American disc jockey, born in Brooklyn, New York, in 1938. He grew up with a large radio that his father gave him and became a fan of R&B and of DJs such as Alan Freed and John R. Richbourg, who later became his mentor. After training in radio and television he worked at small stations and in Shreveport devised the character Wolfman Jack, with a raw voice and sound effects of his own. The character was partly based on the bluesman Howlin' Wolf. His trademark was his hoarse voice, which he himself saw as the basis of his success.

In 1963 he went to the radio station XERF in Ciudad Acuña in Mexico. Those stations, known as border blasters, broadcast at 150,000 watts, three times the American limit, so that they reached almost the whole of North America. There Wolfman Jack developed his style and advertised, among other things, dog food and rose bushes. Later he recorded his programmes in Los Angeles and had the tapes taken across the border. His programme was broadcast by more than two thousand stations in fifty-three countries, including via Armed Forces Radio.

In 1973 he played himself in George Lucas's American Graffiti, which gave him a steady income. From 1973 to 1981 he was the regular host of the TV show The Midnight Special. His voice is mentioned or imitated in songs such as Clap for the Wolfman by The Guess Who. He died in 1995 of a heart attack, shortly after a broadcast. Wolfman Jack turned radio into a nightly party for rock 'n' roll, and the DJ himself into a star.
artiest/wolfman-jack.listen: Listen to Clap for the Wolfman by The Guess Who and notice the voice of Wolfman Jack calling out between the vocals. Can you hear how his raw voice conjures up the atmosphere of a radio broadcast?

artiest/wolter-wierbos.text:
Wolter Wierbos is a Dutch jazz trombonist, born in Holten, Overijssel, in 1957. He has played in Europe, Canada, the United States and Asia and received, among other awards, the Podiumprijs for jazz and improvised music. In 1995 he won the VPRO/Boy Edgar Prize, the most important Dutch jazz award. Since 1979 he has played in numerous groups, such as Cumulus with Ab Baars and Harry de Wit, J.C. Tans & Rockets, the Theo Loevendie Quintet, the Guus Janssen Septet, Peter van Bergen's Loos and the Maarten Altena Ensemble. He also led a group of his own, Celebration of Difference.

Wierbos has worked on theatre, dance, television and film and has been invited by rock bands such as The Ex and Sonic Youth. He has also played with Henry Threadgill, the Berlin Contemporary Jazz Orchestra under Alexander von Schlippenbach, the European Big Band under Cecil Taylor and the Mingus Big Band under Gunther Schuller. He has been active for years with Misha Mengelberg's Instant Composers Pool, which won a Down Beat award in 2002, and with the quintet of Gerry Hemingway and Bik Bent Braam.

He also has a solo career, with, among other things, the project Wollo's World, in which he brings together very different combinations, from a duo with the tap dancer Marije Nie and the bassist Wilbert de Joode to a quartet with Mengelberg, Mats Gustafsson and De Joode. He can be heard on more than a hundred records. His solo CD X Caliber from 1995 shows his instrument from buzzing mutes and growling outbursts to radiant melodies. Wierbos shows that the trombone in Dutch improvised music can sound both funny and adventurous.
artiest/wolter-wierbos.listen: Listen to Wierbos on his solo CD X Caliber and notice the difference between the muted, buzzing sounds and the open melodic passages. Can you hear how many different sounds a single trombone can make?

artiest/wolverine-orchestra.text:
The Wolverines, also called the Wolverine Orchestra, were an American jazz band that in the 1920s were among the most successful regional bands of the Midwest. They first played in September 1923 at the Stockton Club near Hamilton, Ohio. Many of the musicians had come over from Chicago and the leader was the pianist Dudley Mecum. The name came from Wolverine Blues by Jelly Roll Morton, which they often played. At the end of 1923 the cornettist Bix Beiderbecke joined.

On 18 February 1924 they recorded for the first time for Gennett Records, in Richmond, Indiana. On those recordings, which include Jazz Me Blues, Beiderbecke played on a record for the first time. In May 1924 they recorded Free Wheeling by Hoagy Carmichael, which at Beiderbecke's suggestion was renamed Riverboat Shuffle. The group was popular with students, including at Indiana University, and in September 1924 played at the Roseland Ballroom in New York. After that Beiderbecke left the band to play with Jean Goldkette. Jimmy McPartland took his place.

The Wolverines are important above all because Beiderbecke can be heard on them, one of the first great jazz soloists with a soft, lyrical tone. After 1925 the name was used by others, and many jazz revival groups later called themselves Wolverines.
artiest/wolverine-orchestra.listen: Listen to Jazz Me Blues and notice Beiderbecke's cornet. Can you hear how his tone sounds clearer and rounder than you would expect from a jazz band of 1924?

artiest/woody-herman.text:
Woody Herman was born in Milwaukee in 1913. As a child he performed in vaudeville as a singer and tap dancer, and at twelve he played clarinet and saxophone. In 1936 he took over the remains of Isham Jones's orchestra and made his own band out of them. It became known as the band that plays the blues and had its first hit in 1939 with Woodchopper's Ball. In 1942 he reached number one on the Billboard chart with Blues in the Night.

In 1944 he formed the First Herd, a progressive big band with strong influences from Duke Ellington and Count Basie. The orchestra mixed bop themes with swing rhythms and recorded Caldonia in 1945. That year Igor Stravinsky wrote the Ebony Concerto for Herman and his band. In 1947 the Second Herd followed, also known as The Four Brothers Band, after the number Four Brothers, recorded on 27 December 1947 and written by Jimmy Giuffre. The saxophone section consisted of Zoot Sims, Serge Chaloff, Herbie Steward and Stan Getz. Herman led his Herds until his death in 1987 and kept experimenting, right up to jazz rock.

For jazz history he is important above all because his bands often took up new ideas and gave young, gifted players a platform. The saxophone sound of Four Brothers, light and whispering, became a model for West Coast jazz.
artiest/woody-herman.listen: Listen to Four Brothers and notice the saxophone section. Can you hear how the four saxophonists form a single warm sound and then take turns soloing?

artiest/wu-tang-clan.text:
Wu-Tang Clan is a hip hop group from Staten Island in New York, formed in 1992. At its basis were the cousins RZA, GZA and Ol' Dirty Bastard, who had earlier rapped as the All in Together Now Crew. RZA and Ghostface Killah wanted a group with a worldview of its own: Eastern philosophy from kung fu films, the teachings of the Five-Percent Nation and comics. The name came from the film Shaolin and Wu Tang. The other members were Method Man, Raekwon, Inspectah Deck, U-God and Masta Killa, later also Cappadonna. RZA was the leader and the producer.

The self-released single Protect Ya Neck won the group a large underground following. In November 1993 came the debut album Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers), which is regarded as one of the best hip hop albums ever. The contract was unusual: the group signed with Loud Records, but each member was allowed to sign solo with another label. So there followed Method Man's Tical, Raekwon's Only Built 4 Cuban Linx..., GZA's Liquid Swords and Ghostface Killah's Ironman, almost all produced by RZA in his basement studio. Wu-Tang Forever (1997) reached number 1 in America. Ol' Dirty Bastard died in 2004.

The music of Wu-Tang sounded raw and dark: lo-fi beats by RZA with grainy samples and fragments from kung fu films, and rappers who alternate with very different voices and styles. With this approach the group gave new life to the hip hop of the American East Coast, and produced a whole circle of related artists, the Wu-Tang Killa Bees.
artiest/wu-tang-clan.listen: Listen to Protect Ya Neck and notice how the rappers take over from one another after each verse, each with a voice and style of his own. Hear how bare and rough RZA's beat is, with fragments from kung fu films in between.

artiest/wynonie-harris.text:
Wynonie Harris was born in 1915 and grew up in Omaha, Nebraska. As a boy he formed a dance duo, later he performed in clubs, and in Kansas City he listened to blues shouters such as Jimmy Rushing and Big Joe Turner. In 1940 he moved to Los Angeles, where he became known in a club as Mr. Blues. In 1944 he joined Lucky Millinder's orchestra. With the record Who Threw the Whiskey in the Well, released in 1945, he became known to a wide audience, including among white listeners.

As a solo singer he had his greatest success at the label King. There in 1948 he recorded a version of Good Rocking Tonight, the song by Roy Brown from 1947. Harris sang it more energetically, with hand-clapping in gospel style. The song is seen as one of the candidates for the first rock 'n' roll record. Between 1946 and 1952 he had fifteen top ten hits, often with funny and risqué lyrics, such as Lolly Pop Mama and Keep On Churnin'.

Harris was a blues shouter: a singer who had to rise above a band with horns using a hard, loud voice. He died in 1969. His fiery way of singing and his self-assured stage presentation were a model for the first generation of rock 'n' roll singers.
artiest/wynonie-harris.listen: Listen to Good Rocking Tonight and notice the hand claps and the power of his voice. Can you hear how the energy of the song already sounds like rock 'n' roll, even though it is still a blues record?

artiest/wynton-kelly.text:
Wynton Kelly was born in Brooklyn, New York, in 1931, the son of Jamaican immigrants. He began on piano at four, had little formal tuition and from 1943 played professionally in R&B groups. There he learned to play in an accessible, danceable and entertaining way, which continued to colour his style. At sixteen he played on Cornbread by the saxophonist Hal Singer, a number one on the R&B chart. His first album as a leader appeared in 1951. After a period with the singer Dinah Washington and the trumpeter Dizzy Gillespie he was drafted into the army for two years.

Kelly became a sought-after accompanist: he played with Billie Holiday, Cannonball Adderley, John Coltrane, Wes Montgomery and Sonny Rollins. In 1959 he joined Miles Davis's group, replacing Red Garland. On Kind of Blue he plays only on Freddie Freeloader, because Davis had chosen Bill Evans for the rest. He stayed with Davis until 1963, including on Someday My Prince Will Come. With Montgomery he made Full House and Smokin' at the Half Note. His playing was known as lively, bluesy and swinging.

After Davis, Kelly formed his own trio with the bassist Paul Chambers and the drummer Jimmy Cobb, which lasted until 1969. In 1964 Little Tracy from the album Comin' in the Back Door made the R&B chart. Later he had difficulty finding enough work. He suffered from epilepsy and died in a hotel room in Toronto in 1971 after a seizure, aged thirty-nine. Wynton Kelly is regarded as one of the best accompanists in jazz, the pianist who drove a group without getting in its way.
artiest/wynton-kelly.listen: Listen to Freddie Freeloader by Miles Davis and notice Wynton Kelly's piano solo after the trumpet. Can you hear how bluesy and relaxed he plays?

artiest/wynton-marsalis.text: Wynton Marsalis grew up in New Orleans, the son of the pianist Ellis Marsalis. He names Louis Armstrong and Clifford Brown as his great examples. He studied at the Juilliard School and in 1980 played in Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers. In 1984 he won Grammys in both jazz and classical music. He became the face of the Young Lions and argued for acoustic jazz with swing and blues. From 1987 he built up the jazz programme at Lincoln Center in New York, of which he became artistic director. For his oratorio Blood on the Fields he received the Pulitzer Prize for Music in 1997, the first jazz musician to do so.
artiest/wynton-marsalis.listen: Hear the clear, precise trumpet in a quintet in the style of the 1960s.

artiest/x-ray-spex.text:
X-Ray Spex was an English punk band, formed in London in 1976 by the singer Poly Styrene, after she had seen the Sex Pistols live. Styrene, born Marion Elliott-Said, stood out for her singing and her distinctive look and brought in influences from reggae. The band also included Jak Airport on guitar, Paul Dean on bass, B.P. Hurding on drums and Lora Logic on saxophone, an instrument rarely found in punk bands.

The group played twice at The Roxy, and a recording of Oh Bondage Up Yours! appeared on the album Live at the Roxy WC2. In September 1977 the studio version appeared as a single, still their best-known song. It opens with the shouted line that some people think little girls should be seen and not heard. Styrene saw the song as an anti-consumerist number, but it is also seen as a forerunner of riot grrrl. In 1978 came the album Germfree Adolescents, full of criticism of plastic consumer culture, with singles such as Identity and The Day the World Turned Day-Glo. The Guardian praised the album for its anti-consumerist anthems.

In 1979 Styrene left the group, exhausted by touring, and the band broke up. The band later briefly reunited, including with the album Conscious Consumer in 1995. Poly Styrene died in 2011. In a short time the band released five singles and one album and showed that punk could have a voice that was not smoothed over, with a saxophone above the guitars.
artiest/x-ray-spex.listen: Listen to Oh Bondage Up Yours! and notice Poly Styrene's shrieking vocals and the saxophone between the guitars. Can you hear how the sax gives the song a colour of its own?

artiest/xxxtentacion.text:
XXXTENTACION was the stage name of Jahseh Dwayne Ricardo Onfroy, an American rapper, singer and producer, born in Plantation, Florida, in 1998. He began making music on SoundCloud in 2013, after buying a microphone and starting to record with his friend Stokeley Goulbourne, known as Ski Mask the Slump God. His name refers to the Spanish word for temptation. In 2015 he founded the collective Members Only.

The breakthrough came with the single Look at Me, which appeared online in 2016 and entered the American chart in 2017. His first album 17 was released in August 2017 and entered the Billboard 200 at number 2. The second album ? followed in 2018, with Sad! as its lead single. On 18 June 2018 he was shot dead near Deerfield Beach at the age of twenty. Sad! subsequently reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100. The albums SKINS (2018) and Bad Vibes Forever (2019) also appeared after his death.

Musically he refused to be pigeonholed. He mixed rap with distorted bass, heavy guitars, piano melodies and soft, vulnerable singing, and named Kurt Cobain and Tupac Shakur as inspirations. His lyrics were often about depression and loneliness. As a result he is regarded as one of the faces of emo rap and SoundCloud rap, movements that broke through in the second half of the 2010s. His career was short and controversial, partly because of his violent past and the court cases that followed from it, but his influence on a young generation of artists is great.
artiest/xxxtentacion.listen: Listen to Sad! and notice the contrast between the soft, almost gloomy singing and the rhythmic, upbeat accompaniment beneath it. Notice how little is needed to carry the mood.

artiest/yan-huizhu.text:
Yan Huizhu was a Chinese opera singer of Mongolian descent, born in 1919. She performed in two genres of Chinese musical theatre: jingju, Peking opera, and kunqu. Her father, Yan Jupeng, was himself a jingju actor and had developed a singing style of his own. He tried to keep her from the demanding profession, but she learned songs and roles while he was on tour. In 1937 she joined a theatre company under the name Huizhu.

The famous master Mei Lanfang took her under his wing when he was not allowed to perform during the Japanese occupation of Beijing. Because of that bond she was nicknamed Little Mei Lanfang. In February 1946 she had a great success with the opera Shengsi hen in Beijing, and from then on she was called the Queen of Peking Opera. After the founding of the People's Republic in 1949 she continued to perform. In 1957 she became deputy director of the School of Traditional Opera in Shanghai, where she taught the Mei style, and she toured Europe. With Yu Zhenfei she often performed an adapted version of Qiangtou mashang. In 1960 they married.

Peking opera combines singing, gesture, acrobatics and a sharp, high use of the voice with percussion and strings. Yan Huizhu was one of the women who gave that art a new face in the twentieth century. Her life ended tragically: during the Cultural Revolution she was attacked and denounced by the Red Guards, and on the night of 10 September 1966 she took her own life.
artiest/yan-huizhu.listen: Listen to an extract from a Peking opera recording and notice the voice: how high and tense it sounds, and how the percussion accompanies every gesture of the singer.

artiest/yann-tiersen.text: Yann Tiersen was born in Brest in Brittany in 1970. He was taught piano and violin at music schools in Rennes, Nantes and Boulogne-sur-Mer, but as a teenager he chose punk and the electric guitar. Later he played many different instruments: toy piano, accordion, harpsichord, music boxes and even a typewriter. The director Jean-Pierre Jeunet heard his albums and used existing pieces alongside new work for Le fabuleux destin d'Amélie Poulain (2001). That music won a César. For Good Bye, Lenin! (2003) he wrote an entirely new score. After that came, among other things, the documentary Tabarly (2008). His style is often compared with that of Philip Glass and Michael Nyman. He recorded many albums on the island of Ushant.
artiest/yann-tiersen.listen: Notice the repeated patterns in the accompaniment and the waltz rhythms, and the sound of instruments such as the accordion, toy piano and piano.

artiest/yared.text:
Yared is the name of a saint from ancient Ethiopia, who according to tradition lived in the sixth century in the kingdom of Aksum. The Ethiopian Orthodox Church regards him as the founder of its church chant. That tradition is called zema and is sung to this day in the churches of Ethiopia. What is known of his life rests on legend and church tradition, not on documents from his own time.

According to that tradition Yared arranged the chants of the church in three modes, called Geez, Ezel and Araray. They are linked with the seasons of the year. He is also said to have devised a notation system of his own, with signs placed above and below the text of the chants that indicate the movement of the melody. In this way Ethiopian church chant is among the oldest music traditions that have survived to the present. The singing is accompanied by percussion, such as the kebero drum, and the sistrum, a rhythmically rattling instrument, and by the movement of prayer sticks, with which the singers mark the rhythm.

For the history of pop, Yared is important above all as a source and as a reminder: long before sound recordings existed, there was already a music culture with its own modes and its own notation. The church singing tradition of Ethiopia continues to work through in the way Ethiopian musicians later thought about melody and scale.
artiest/yared.listen: Listen to a recording of Ethiopian church chant and notice how the singers and the rhythmic percussion alternate. Try to hear how the melody moves forward in small steps.

artiest/yasiin-bey.text:
Yasiin Bey was born Dante Terrell Smith in Brooklyn, New York, in 1973, and became known under the name Mos Def, short for most definitely. In 2011 he had his name officially changed. Yasiin is the name of the thirty-sixth sura of the Quran, and he said that all his life he had wanted to be seen as a person, not as a product. Before his music career he was a child actor in television films and series. In 1994 he began rapping in the group Urban Thermo Dynamics, together with his brother and sister.

In 1996 he began as a soloist and worked with De La Soul and Da Bush Babees. At the label Rawkus Records he formed the duo Black Star with Talib Kweli. Their album Mos Def & Talib Kweli Are Black Star came out in 1998, largely produced by Hi-Tek. His solo debut Black on Both Sides appeared in 1999. The New Danger followed in 2004, with his rock band Black Jack Johnson, True Magic in 2006 and The Ecstatic in 2009, on which Madlib provided much of the production. Later came Negus and, with Black Star, the record No Fear of Time in 2022. He also collaborated with Kanye West, The Roots and Gorillaz.

Bey is regarded as an important name in conscious hip hop. His lyrics are rich in wordplay and deal with political and social subjects, such as police violence and the position of African Americans. His style cannot be pinned down: he sings and raps, draws on soul, jazz and rock, and also played a large number of film roles. In doing so he showed that a rapper can be much more than a rapper.
artiest/yasiin-bey.listen: Listen to Stylo by Gorillaz, on which Bey has a guest role alongside Bobby Womack. Notice how his calm, almost spoken voice sits next to the electronic beat and the soul singing.

artiest/yasunori-mitsuda.text:
Yasunori Mitsuda was born in Tokuyama, Japan, in 1972 and grew up in Yamaguchi Prefecture. As a child he had piano lessons, but gave them up quickly, because he preferred sport. At secondary school he wanted to become a composer, inspired by Vangelis's film music for Blade Runner and by Henry Mancini. He studied at the Junior College of Music in Tokyo and in 1992 joined the games company Square, where at first he mainly made sound effects for games such as Final Fantasy V and Secret of Mana.

In 1994 he demanded to be allowed to compose, and so he got Chrono Trigger, released in 1995. He was the only composer and wrote 54 pieces. He worked so hard that he developed stomach ulcers, after which Nobuo Uematsu finished the work. Mitsuda attributes the success to influences from folk and jazz rather than the semi-symphonic style that was then usual in game music. He then composed Xenogears in 1998 and Chrono Cross in 1999. In 1998 he became a freelancer and in 2001 he founded Procyon Studio, with the label Sleigh Bells. Later he also wrote for Xenosaga, Shadow Hearts and the anime Inazuma Eleven.

His music is regarded as among the best in the history of computer games. It shows that a small sliver of sound from a games console can tell a full, melodic story.
artiest/yasunori-mitsuda.listen: Listen to the music of Chrono Trigger and notice the melody, which is built from short, repeated motifs. Can you hear folk or jazz influences beneath the electronic sounds?

artiest/yazoo.text:
Yazoo was an English synth-pop duo from Basildon, in Essex. The keyboard player Vince Clarke and the singer Alison Moyet started it at the end of 1981, shortly after Clarke had left Depeche Mode. Moyet had placed an advertisement in a music paper: she was looking for musicians for a blues band. The only reply came from Clarke, who was looking for someone to record his new song Only You with. They came from the same town, but barely knew each other. They borrowed the name from the blues record label Yazoo Records. In America they were called Yaz, because the name was already taken there.

The two had very different tastes. Moyet liked blues and punk, Clarke electronic music such as that of OMD. It was precisely that combination that made Yazoo special: Clarke's cool, tight synthesizer patterns beneath Moyet's warm, powerful soul voice. Only You became a big hit in Britain in 1982, as did Don't Go. The debut album Upstairs at Eric's (1982) was named after the studio owner Eric Radcliffe, who co-produced it. In New York the DJ François Kevorkian made a club remix of Situation, which caught on in the dance clubs.

The duo worked mainly alongside each other, not with each other. For the second album, You and Me Both (1983), they were rarely in the studio at the same time, and shortly afterwards they split up. Moyet began a successful solo career, Clarke went on with The Assembly and Erasure. In 2008 they came together one more time for a tour. Yazoo helped to shape synth-pop and had a great influence on the house music of the 1980s.
artiest/yazoo.listen: Listen to Don't Go from 1982. Notice Vince Clarke's sharp, repeated synthesizer motif and how Alison Moyet's full voice sets itself warmly against it.

artiest/yeah-yeah-yeahs.text:
Yeah Yeah Yeahs is an American indie rock band that formed in New York in 2000. The singer Karen O and the guitarist Nick Zinner began as an acoustic duo under the name Unitard and changed that name to Yeah Yeah Yeahs. They chose a messy, punk-like sound. A day before a gig supporting The White Stripes, Karen O brought in the drummer Brian Chase, because she did not want a drum machine live. He stayed, and so the group became a trio without a bassist.

In 2001 their first EP appeared on their own label Shifty. They financed the debut album Fever to Tell, from 2003, themselves, because major labels would not give them creative freedom. Dave Sitek of TV on the Radio became co-producer. From the album came Maps, their best-known song. Show Your Bones followed in 2006, It's Blitz! in 2009, Mosquito in 2013 and Cool It Down in 2022. The sound developed from raw garage rock into more electronic, danceable pop.

The group belongs to the rock revival of the early 2000s, in which garage rock and post-punk returned. Karen O was known for her bubbling live performances and her voice, which could go from whispering to screaming. Rolling Stone places Fever to Tell and Maps on its lists of the best albums and songs of all time.
artiest/yeah-yeah-yeahs.listen: Listen to Maps and notice Karen O's singing. Can you hear how the song works towards the chorus with soft, vulnerable sounds, rather than with force?
